stories.headline: Brazil’s presidential election heads to a runoff after Flávio Bolsonaro finishes ahead of President Lula in the first round

sources.body:
Right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro has won the first round of Brazil's presidential election, beating left-wing President Lula da Silva, but falling short of an outright majority.

There will be a run-off between the two candidates on 25 October.

Bolsonaro is the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup after losing the 2022 election.

Sunday's vote was close, with President Lula polling slightly ahead during the campaign. With almost all of the votes counted, Bolsonaro has 47% to Lula's 45% of the vote.

Bolsonaro's result exceeded expectations, meaning the second round now looks like his to lose, given some of the other candidates knocked out in the first round were right-wing alternatives.

Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL) also had the most governors, senators and federal deputies elected in the results so far, meaning the party is expected to have the most influence in Congress.

The majority of Latin America has now elected right-wing presidents, aligned to the Trump administration, and the run-off will determine whether Brazil – Latin America's largest country and economy – will follow suit.

After casting his ballot, Lula, 80, warned the choice was between democracy and "barbarism".

Bolsonaro, 45, said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people".

Lula and Bolsonaro are the two biggest names in Brazilian politics, on the left and right, and this campaign has polarised Brazil yet again: with themes of sovereignty, crime, the economy and corruption being top concerns for voters.

Lula is more popular in Brazil's poorer northeast, among low-income voters, Catholics, and women.

He is seeking a fourth term in office, after being elected in 2002, 2006 and then a later non-consecutive term in 2022. In that election, he beat Jair Bolsonaro by less than 2% of the vote, the closest presidential election result in Brazil's history.

After that election, Bolsonaro's supporters vandalised government buildings on 8 January 2023.

Jair Bolsonaro was banned from running for re-election even before his prison sentence, but endorsed his eldest son Flávio to run in his place. Jair Bolsonaro's wife, Michelle, was elected to the Senate on Sunday.

Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to grant his father, and his supporters responsible for the 8 January riots, amnesty if elected.

He is more popular in the south, and among wealthier voters and evangelical Christians.

Bolsonaro said on Sunday he was "very happy" to have led Lula in the first-round vote, and expressed confidence that he would clinch a run-off victory in three weeks' time.

"I am very happy with the real possibility that, three weeks from now, Brazil will give a definitive answer by choosing a modern government," he said, according to AFP.

Lula said the outcome of the vote was "unexpected", but insisted the race was not over.

"I admit I was convinced I would win in the first round," he said on Sunday. "The game is about to start. We are in extra time. In extra time, we will win over the Brazilian people."
sources.headline: Right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round of Brazil election

sources.body:
Far-right challenger and son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro put in a stronger than expected showing, with Lula calling the result ‘unexpected’

Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff.

With 99.9% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival. Lula received 45.1%. Bolsonaro received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m.

Bolsonaro will go into the second round as strong favourite and is likely to be boosted by the migration of votes from the election’s other rightwing candidates, who included Ronaldo Caiado, who secured 2.1%, and Renan Santos, who won 2.2%.

Brazil’s far-right put in an even stronger than expected showing, with a succession of Bolsonarista politicians winning congressional or gubernatorial races. They included Jair Bolsonaro’s second son, Carlos Bolsonaro, and his wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, who both won seats in the senate. Bolsonaro’s youngest son, Jair Renan, was elected to the lower house of congress. Bolsonaro’s former infrastructure minister, Tarcísio de Freitas, was reelected as governor of São Paulo, Brazil’s most populous and economically important state.

Of the 54 senators elected, 34 were from the right or far right.

Flávio Bolsonaro told supporters in the capital, Brasília, that the result signalled “the end of an era” for Lula’s Workers’ party. “Lula has fought seven presidential elections. He’s worried about power. I am worried about the future of Brazil,” he said.

​Speaking in Sāo Paulo, Lula put a brave face on a difficult night for the left. “We have just had a lesson in Brazilian democracy,” he said. “The result is often unexpected. We can never get everything we wanted. I confess to you that I was convinced I was going to win the election in the first round … But we have a second round.” Lula said Bolsonaro’s “dark past” would become clearer to voters in the lead-up to that vote. “From tomorrow we will launch a new campaign: [and in] a campaign with only two candidates we will be able to show the difference between our proposals for Brazil.”

Earlier, as he cast this vote, Lula said Latin America’s largest democracy faced a stark choice, highlighting his adversary’s well-documented links to members of Rio’s underworld , including once employing close relatives of a notorious contract killer.

Lula, who became Brazil’s first elected working-class president in 2002 and was returned to office in 2006 and 2022, is hoping to secure a historic fourth non-consecutive term in this year’s election.

Allies of the veteran leftwinger called the election a crucial battle in the fight against a far-right movement that less than four years ago brought chaos to the capital, Brasília, during an unsuccessful attempt to overturn the result of the 2022 election, when Lula beat the incumbent president, Jair Bolsonaro.
sources.headline: Brazil’s presidential race goes to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula

sources.body:
Flavio Bolsonaro beat polling expectations as Brazil’s right gained ground, setting up October 25 run-off with Lula.

Brazil’s closely watched presidential election is heading to a second round between leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, prolonging a deeply polarised race with major implications for the country and the wider region.

Brazil’s electoral court confirmed on Sunday that the two candidates will advance to a run-off on October 25 after neither won the majority needed to secure the presidency outright, with Bolsonaro leading at 56 million votes to Lula’s almost 53 million.

Lula, 80, is seeking a fourth, non-consecutive term after a political career spanning nearly five decades.

Bolsonaro, 45, is the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro and is trying to return his father’s right-wing movement to power, even as the former president serves a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election.

The election comes at a pivotal time for Latin America’s largest economy. Brazilians are grappling with concerns over crime and the cost of living, while the country faces an increasingly tense relationship with the United States. The vote is also being closely watched across a region that has shifted sharply to the right in a series of recent elections.

While a second round was widely expected, the first-round result did not play out quite as pollsters had predicted.

Here are some of the key takeaways from the election so far.

With nearly 99 percent of votes reported, Bolsonaro had about 47 percent of valid votes, compared with 44.9 percent for Lula. Neither reached the 50 percent threshold needed to win in the first round.

That sets up another Lula-Bolsonaro showdown, four years after Lula narrowly defeated former President Jair Bolsonaro. This time, he will face the former president’s eldest son.

The race could be extremely close, as polling ahead of Sunday’s vote suggested Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro were roughly tied in a potential run-off.

That puts voters who backed one of the other 10 candidates in the first round at the centre of the fight for the presidency over the next three weeks.

Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos, who together received about 5.3 million votes, have previously said they will not endorse either candidate in the run-off.

Most polls leading up to election day predicted the race would be pushed into the second round, but had Lula finishing the first round ahead of Bolsonaro.

Instead, Bolsonaro emerged with a lead of two percentage points, raising questions about why the final polls underestimated his support.

On Sunday, Bolsonaro said the results showed that Brazilians want change.

Analysts told the Reuters news agency that Bolsonaro may have benefitted from “protest votes” from people who may have preferred another candidate but saw defeating Lula as the priority. Many had been expected to shift their support to Bolsonaro only in a second round, meaning this could have consequences for his support in three weeks.
sources.headline: Brazil’s presidential race: Three key takeaways from the first round

stories.headline: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches a major offensive against Houthi-held territory

sources.body:
The announcement came hours after Iranian-backed Houthis reportedly cut a vital supply route to besieged city of Taiz

Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has announced the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis , even as the militant group made fresh gains on the ground, reportedly encircling a government-held city.

Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement on Sunday: “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory.”

The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait – a chokepoint for international shipping – after a lightning offensive by the Iran-backed Houthis.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia . The Houthis have increasingly targeted Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, and on Sunday said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital again.

The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital, Aden, according to four security sources.

The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around the city.

“We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area said.

Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. Fighting in the area was ongoing, they added.

Sources from both sides told AFP on Sunday that fighting in and around the western province of Taiz had killed more than 70 people over the past day.

Sources from the internationally recognised government reported that 34 government troops were killed – 20 on the edge of Taiz province in neighbouring Lahj – while Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in border areas with Lahj.

Taiz city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s long-running civil war.

A Houthi military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said on Sunday the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy company Aramco’s sites in Riyadh and in Khurais area in the east, causing large fires.

The attacks were in response to what the Houthis claimed were 50 Saudi-led ‌air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours.

There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.

Saudi oil exports were already under pressure due to Iran’s blockade of the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

The Houthi’s Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes on Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded.
sources.headline: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches military drive to retake all Houthi-held territory

sources.body:
After launching major military offensive to reclaim Houthi-held areas, Yemen’s government says it has retaken a key district.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has announced a major military campaign to retake all territory controlled by the Houthis, marking a new escalation in a civil war that had largely been frozen for several years before battles intensified in recent weeks.

The announcement by Rashad al-Alimi, chairman of the Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), the executive body of the Yemeni government, comes after weeks of heavy fighting and major Houthi advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and around the strategically important city of Taiz.

On Monday, Yemeni government forces said they were launching a “strategic” offensive on the country’s capital, Sanaa, which the Houthis have held since 2014.

Earlier in the day, the Yemeni forces — who are backed by Saudi Arabia — said they had regained control of the Dhubab district on the country’s west coast near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, though the Houthis denied the announcement.

The fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah, meaning Supporters of God in Arabic – and Yemeni government forces has expanded since a fragile 2022 truce collapsed in July, displacing more than 100,000 people since then.

Last month, the Houthis launched a rapid offensive that captured about 150km (93 miles) of Red Sea coastline and areas around Bab al-Mandeb, the narrow waterway connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, which is a critical route for international shipping.

On Monday, the foreign minister of Yemen’s internationally recognised government requested more support from the international community to defeat the Houthis, saying it is “in the world’s interest” for the country to be stable.

“We call upon our brothers, friends and the international community to support the Yemeni people, their state, and their national institutions in confronting the terrorist Houthi militia, which seizes their will by force of arms and lays waste to the lives of their sons – after exhausting all opportunities for de-escalation and peace,” Afrah al-Zouba said in a post on X.

So what is the latest on the fighting, and what does Yemen’s government hope to achieve?

The Yemeni government army said on Monday 1,747 Houthi fighters had been “neutralised” in 1,122 military operations in the Saada, al-Jawf and Taiz governorates and along Yemen’s western coast.

Military spokesman Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili said the attacks targeted artillery and rocket positions, fortifications, supply lines, reinforcements and command centres.

Al-Nuzaili said warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and snipers were involved and 364 military and logistical vehicles had been destroyed or disabled. The casualty and equipment figures could not be independently verified.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government also announced that its forces had taken control of Dhubab on the Red Sea coast and were launching a major offensive on Sanaa.
sources.headline: Yemen war: What’s the latest, as government forces claim advances?

sources.body: The Yemeni military, backed by Saudi jets, began a broad set of strikes on Monday against Iran-backed Houthi targets in an attempt to retake lost territory. The Houthis launched an offensive in September, which killed hundreds of combatants on both sides, according to UN figures, and has since become the most active front in the wider Middle East war.
sources.headline: Yemen, Saudi Arabia launch new strikes against Houthis in bid to retake lost territory

stories.headline: Ethiopian forces retake Mekelle as fighting resumes in Tigray

sources.body:
Rebel forces in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region have said they have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with the national army moves towards the city.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which has been running the region, said it decised to leave because of concerns about risks to civilians.

Two Mekelle residents told the BBC that pro-government forces now control the city and TPLF fighters have abandoned it. One resident also said mobile phone services had been restored.

Fighting has erupted in recent weeks between the TPLF and allied groups and government forces in parts of the northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

TPLF chairman Debretsion Gebremichael said that while they were leaving Mekelle for the timebeing, the conflict remained fluid and the group would "continue its work from another location".

He described it as a deliberate strategic move, saying: "We will attack the enemy where we choose, not where he chooses for us."

During the 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray, the TPLF made a similar move and resorted to guerrilla attacks after losing control of Mekelle to federal forces.

The latest outbreak of fighting has raised concerns among observers that the conflict could further destabilise the Horn of Africa, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries.

The US Department of State called for "restraint" and "dialogue" on all sides ahead of a diplomatic meeting about the conflict in Egypt with leaders from some of Ethiopia's neighbours.

The presidents of Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan - which all have strained relations with Ethiopia - met on Sunday in the Egyptian coastal city of El-Alamein.

They called for "respecting the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of states" and the resolution of disputes through "peaceful means".

Ethiopia accuses Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan of supporting the Tigray rebels, which they deny.

Duke Burbridge, an American doctor with the Health Professionals Network for Tigray, told the BBC that the situation had been calm since the rebels pulled out, except for some outbreaks of gunfire and looting shortly after the withdrawal.

He said it "appeared some people who were released from prison or some of the criminal gangs around here [who] were well armed" were involved.

Telecommunication services, which had been cut, had now been restored, he said.

"[Yesterday] everybody was in the restaurants, in the markets, enjoying the fact that cell phones were back on, mobile banking was back on, and there was loud music deep into the night," he told the BBC Newsday programme.

Burbridge said some relative normality was returning, although some food items, including fruits and vegetables, were not available.

Tigray residents have been trying to recover from a devastating two-year civil war that ended in 2022 when the African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides.

However, in the last six months there has been a worsening of relations, with both sides accusing each other of violating the agreement.
sources.headline: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital

sources.body:
The capture of Tigray’s regional capital revives fears of another prolonged conflict, displacement and crisis.

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia – The capture of Tigray’s regional capital Mekelle by Ethiopian federal forces and allied Tigray Peace Force fighters has revived painful memories of the 2020–22 Tigray war, with residents fearing a return to prolonged violence, displacement and economic hardship.

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) confirmed on Saturday that it had withdrawn from Mekelle, saying its regional administration would temporarily operate from another location. Government forces and allied fighters entered the city on Saturday, with a pro-government militia source, a humanitarian worker and a Mekelle resident confirming to the Reuters news agency on Sunday that they were in control of the city.

The development comes less than four years after the Ethiopian government and the TPLF signed the Pretoria agreement that ended two years of devastating fighting.

Berihu, a 32-year-old bajaj driver in Shire, northwestern Tigray, said the latest fighting had been particularly difficult to watch.

“I feel very heartbroken knowing that Tigray has gone back to full-scale war,” he said in a phone interview with Al Jazeera. “We have already seen what the last war did to our people, and now it feels like we are going through it all over again.”

The 2020–22 war killed hundreds of thousands of people, according to estimates, displaced millions and caused extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods.

The African Union-facilitated agreement, signed in Pretoria in November 2022, ended the large-scale fighting, but key issues, including the status of disputed territories, the return of displaced people and the disarmament of Tigrayan forces, remained unresolved.

In July, the TPLF said the Pretoria agreement had effectively collapsed, accusing the federal government of failing to implement key provisions. The federal government rejected that characterisation, saying it remained committed to the peace process while accusing the TPLF of undermining the agreement.

The political dispute was accompanied by growing military tensions, including reports of sporadic clashes and drone strikes in parts of Tigray. The two sides also traded accusations over troop movements and preparations for renewed fighting.

The capture of Mekelle marks a major development in the renewed conflict, putting the city once again at the centre of the fighting.

In Addis Ababa, the developments have also alarmed residents who remember the consequences of the previous war.

Abel, a 30-year-old shopkeeper, said the fighting had felt distant until explosions were heard in the capital .

“I woke up and heard that my city had been hit,” he said. “You hear about fighting in Tigray, and it feels far away. But when you hear about explosions in Addis Ababa, you start asking yourself what will happen next.”

Diplomatic sources said explosions were heard in several parts of the capital, including near the headquarters of Ethiopia’s military. Reuters separately reported that a source linked to an opposition alliance claimed the group had carried out drone strikes in Addis Ababa, including against military facilities. The claim could not be independently verified.
sources.headline: Ethiopia’s forces retake Mekelle amid renewed Tigray fighting

stories.headline: The United States withdraws B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain after a suspected terror plot nearby

sources.body:
The US has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, the UK military base at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter-terror police.

A statement from a Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday it had removed its bombers - thought to be about a dozen B-1s - from the base back to their home stations in America.

US media reported a new threat led to the bombers being removed, which follows a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.

Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences and subsequently released on bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail.

Whitehall officials have confirmed that in relation to the threats they are currently dealing with "there is an ongoing high tempo of threat from Iran to the UK, and it's logical that US airbases would be pretty high on any targeting list".

They have also not disputed the decision from Washington was in response to the incident at the airbase in Gloucestershire.

The BBC has also been told it was a military rather than a political decision - taken at an operational level - and communicated from the US military to its British counterparts.

The UK's Ministry of Defence has not commented.

Tracking websites showed B-1 bombers flying out of RAF Fairford on Sunday.

The New York Times reported US commanders had received new threats about an Iran-backed plot against RAF Fairford according to two US officials.

The newspaper wrote the new information was part of the same threat warnings from three weeks ago, but officials acted quickly after specific details emerged in the past 24 hours.

The planes reportedly took off while aerial refueling aircraft were still being scrambled to support their flights to the US.

Days after the incident at RAF Fairford, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident but did not provide further details. Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

Initially, five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF). All five were UK nationals from London.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

The sixth man, aged 25, was arrested in London on Thursday on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. Counter terror police confirmed on Saturday he had also been released on bail.

RAF Fairford, nearby the village of Whelford in the Cotswolds, has been used as a forward operating location by the USAF for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

Residents living close to RAF Fairford told the BBC of their relief at the departure of bombers from the airbase, with one villager saying she was "thrilled" citing the noise and feeling "increasingly vulnerable" in recent weeks.
sources.headline: US air force removes all bombers from British military base RAF Fairford

sources.body: Royal Air Force Fairford has been used by the U.S. for long-range bombing missions in its war against Iran.

stories.headline: The Nobel Prize in Medicine is awarded for research enabling control of neurons with light

sources.body:
US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their work in the field of optogenetics.

Their research has helped scientists learn more about the inner workings of the brain, to better understand how the human mind works.

The Nobel Committee praised the trio for laying the foundation of a new era in neuroscience by revealing how to switch on and off neural circuits behind "specific memories, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders".

In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method to try to restore sight in people with visual impairment .

"Optogenetics has fundamentally altered our understanding of the brain," the Nobel Assembly said.

"Every day brings new discoveries, helping to solve one of humanity's great mysteries: how our incredible brain works."

The winners said it was "absolutely wonderful" to get the award, and that it was an honour to share the accolade with friends.

The three men will also share the £900,000 (12 million Swedish kronor) prize money.

Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, explained: "Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of."

Before, the inner workings behind feelings, behaviours and bodily functions were more of a mystery to scientists.

Optogentics is a way to illuminate brain pathways, using a special protein borrowed from algae that scientists use to control cell electrical activity using light.

In the early 2000s, Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, the algal protein with unique properties.

Deisseroth worked out how to use this light controlled protein to switch on nerve cells in the brains of mice.

Researchers have since been able to study nerve cells and pathways in animals to see and discover more about what they do.

The Nobel Committee said: "Using light, researchers are now able to switch individual neural circuits on or off in the brain. They can bring memories to life, create feelings, drive behaviours and study the types of neurons that are involved in various psychiatric and neurological disorders."

That is providing important insights into how the nervous system interacts with various cells in other areas of the body, such as in the heart and gut, the committee added.

Researchers have also taken "the first steps" towards using optogenetics as a medical treatment, the committee explained.

In ongoing clinical trials, scientists have been working to restore vision in people who have become blind due to retinitis pigmentosa, a disease that destroys the eye's rods and cones.

By inserting a special protein in the damaged region of the eye, the patient regained some vision when wearing special glasses emitting light. This switched on the therapeutic algae proteins.
sources.headline: Nobel Prize awarded for showing inner workings of the brain

sources.body:
Three scientists to share 12m Swedish kronor prize for their work on ‘light-gated ion channels and optogenetics’

The Nobel prize in physiology or medicine 2026 has been awarded to three scientists for their work on investigating the mysteries of the brain.

Karl Deisseroth of both Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University, Peter Hegemann of the Humboldt University of Berlin, and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg have been awarded the prize “for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.”.

The Nobel assembly at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden , announced the winners on Monday. They will share a prize of 12m Swedish kronor (about £901,500).

The 2026 award is the 117th time the prize has been given. Out of the 235 laureates – including the latest winners – only 14 have been women.
sources.headline: Nobel prize in medicine 2026 awarded for research into mysteries of brain

stories.headline: A Flydubai co-pilot is accused of planning to crash an aircraft into Tel Aviv airport or a building

sources.body:
The co-pilot accused of trying to hijack a flydubai plane planned to crash the aircraft into Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion airport or a tower block in the Israeli city, US and Israeli reports suggest.

The Omani national was a "lone wolf" extremist, according to the reports.

The United Arab Emirates' attorney-general has said the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act" on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv last Wednesday.

He attacked and wounded the captain with the emergency crash axe kept in the cockpit before being overpowered by passengers. Another crew travelling on the plane was able to land it in Saudi Arabia.

Israel's prime minister has said the co-pilot underwent "Islamist radical indoctrination" and the captain, passengers and a second crew prevented "a 9/11 disaster".

More details about the co-pilot of the flydubai flight – whom multiple reports have named as Hamam al-Hammami – emerged over the weekend as he continued to be questioned in the UAE, with Israeli representatives being updated.

Israeli media cited sources with knowledge of the probe as saying the co-pilot told investigators that, having attacked Capt Smit Machchhar, he intended to continue flying the plane as normal into Israeli airspace and receive landing clearances from Ben Gurion airport.

He then planned to crash the Boeing 737 MAX – with more than 180 passengers on board – into the airport or into a tower block in central Tel Aviv, in the style of al-Qaeda's 11 September 2001 attacks in the US, according to the reports.

The sources are quoted as saying he was most likely to have acted alone rather than on behalf of a radical organisation or foreign government.

The co-pilot also reportedly told investigators that he had intended to hijack and crash a previous flight to Tel Aviv but changed his mind because he knew someone on board.

There was no immediate comment from Emirati or Israeli authorities.

UAE Attorney-General Hamad al-Shamsi said on Saturday that his country's investigations would establish the full circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident, and that the results would be announced upon their conclusion.

Questions are also being asked about major security lapses, including how the attacker was recruited by flydubai and given clearance to fly a plane filled with Israelis to Tel Aviv.

Regional officials said the co-pilot was barred from flying by Oman's national carrier, Oman Air, and moved to an administrative job because of concerns about his extremist views.

He was later hired by UAE-based flydubai after undergoing standard security checks that did not examine his background for potential signs of radicalisation, according to the officials.

Israeli aviation regulations also state that pilots who are citizens of countries without formal diplomatic relations with Israel, like Oman, are not permitted to operate flights to the country.

Regional officials told the Associated Press on Sunday that Emirati authorities had shared with Israel a list of passengers and crew ahead of flight FZ1073's departure.
sources.headline: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport or building, reports say

sources.body:
RMIT confirms co-pilot was a student as Australian authorities examine his time in country between 2015 and 2017

An Australian university has confirmed a flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound flight studied at its Melbourne campus, but left before completing his qualification.

Disaster was narrowly averted on 30 September when passengers and crew intervened to stop the alleged attempt of the co-pilot, identified by media outlets as Hammam al-Hammami, to take control of a flight to Tel Aviv with 182 people onboard.

The United ⁠Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general said the co-pilot allegedly used a crash axe in the attempted “terrorist attack”, in which the pilot was stabbed mid-air. Numerous media outlets have named the co-pilot al-Hammami, an Omani national.

On Monday, the RMIT university in Melbourne said in a statement that it “is aware of media reporting of a former student alleged to be involved in the Flydubai flight incident”.

“The individual was enrolled at RMIT but did not successfully complete an engineering qualification,” the university

“As this is an ongoing investigation, the University is unable to provide further comment.”

Former RMIT engineering students contacted by Guardian Australia said they did not remember al-Hammami.

RMIT university’s confirmation came after the Australian federal police (AFP) on Sunday said agencies were investigating the man’s time in the country.

A source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, has said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014, before arriving in the country to commence a university course the next year.

He left Australia in 2017, and his visa was cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed he was no longer enrolled in the course, the source said.

The AFP on Sunday said multiple agencies – including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (Asio) – were probing the man’s connections to the country.

“The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team (VIC JCTT), comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO, can confirm it is investigating the man’s links to Australia,” an AFP spokesperson said.

“An update will be provided at an appropriate time.”

Court records and previous media reporting show that a number of Australians charged with terror offences or suspected of Islamic extremism studied at RMIT around the same time as al-Hammami, but there was no indication he knew any of these individuals.

A British university, Buckinghamshire New University, has confirmed a student named Hamam al-Hammami had “previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management”. It added: “He did not undertake any pilot training at the university.”

A flydubai spokesperson on Saturday said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still ‌under investigation and the airline was not in a position to comment further.

The airline’s flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv were suspended after the attack. The Omani co-pilot and the flight’s Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, were taken to the UAE, as it leads the investigation. Officials have said a number of countries including Israel are participating.
sources.headline: Alleged flydubai attacker left Australia without finishing engineering course, university says

Imagen de archivo de un avión de Flydubai con pasajeros procedentes de Tabuk (Arabia Saudí) aterrizando en el Aeropuerto Internacional Ben Gurión, cerca de Tel Aviv (Israel), el 30 de septiembre de 2026. / ABIR SULTAN / EFE

El atacante omaní del vuelo de Flydubai confirma a los investigadores que su objetivo principal era estrellar el avión en el principal aeropuerto de Israel en Tel Aviv, a donde se dirigía la aeronave. También ha confesado que tenía este plan desde antes de empezar a trabajar para la compañía emiratí. Mientras tanto, en Israel se vive un intercambio de acusaciones entre las agencias de seguridad y el ministerio de Transporte , al que el Shin Bet culpa de ignorar sus avisos para mejorar los controles en vuelos internacionales. La oposición ha pedido la dimisión de la ministra Miri Regev y el primer ministro, Binyamín Netanyahu , ha ordenado al Consejo Nacional de Seguridad (CNS) que revise las directrices de aviación.

También esta petición ha levantado ampollas. El exjefe del CNS, Eyal Hulata , ha criticado duramente la "revisión" ordenada por Netanyahu, calificándola de "ritual" vacío e insistiendo en que el primer ministro tiene la máxima responsabilidad sobre el asunto . Aunque, en un primer momento del ataque del miércoles, el mandatario israelí lo vio como una oportunidad para sacar rédito político al haberse evitado una catástrofe , el discurso va cambiando a medida que se conocen más detalles de cómo logró el copiloto omaní, Hamam al Hammami , de 29 años, llegar a pilotar un avión civil camino a Israel. Al Hammami ha confesado que iba a estrellar el avión en otro vuelo de la misma ruta que realizó en julio , pero que se hizo atrás al darse cuenta que un amigo suyo estaba entre la tripulación.

Su intención era continuar con el vuelo 1073 de Flydubai con normalidad tras deshacerse del capitán, obtener todas las autorizaciones de aterrizaje necesarias y, posteriormente, estrellarse contra un edificio o un avión en el aeropuerto Ben Gurion, según informaron medios de comunicación hebreos. Al esperar hasta el último momento, habría evitado que nadie se diera cuenta de lo que estaba sucediendo, dando la voz de alarma e impidiendo que llevara a cabo su plan. Sus ideas se vieron frustradas cuando el piloto indio, Smit Machchhar , pese a estar malherido, logró abrir la puerta de la cabina y los pasajeros israelíes entraron y redujeron al atacante, evitando la tragedia y aterrizando de emergencia en Arabia Saudí gracias a la presencia a bordo de dos pilotos fuera de servicio.

De momento, los investigadores israelíes no han interrogado personalmente a Al Hammami, que se encuentra en Emiratos Árabes Unidos . La información ha sido transmitida a Israel por las investigaciones saudí y emiratí . También las autoridades australianas están investigando sus vínculos con Australia , ya que estudió en una universidad pública de aviación en Melbourne. Al copiloto, se le prohibió hace dos años volar para la compañía nacional omaní porque le encontraron material extremista . Esta revelación provocó una lluvia de críticas contra el Ministerio de Transporte. El Gobierno, Regev y el ministerio negaron toda responsabilidad, al defender que no tienen la capacidad de realizar verificaciones de antecedentes a los pilotos extranjeros y que no existe forma de garantizar de manera definitiva la seguridad de los vuelos internacionales a Israel. Sin embargo, documentos internos del CNS indican que altos organismos israelíes llevan años advirtiendo que el ministerio no ha estado cumpliendo con sus responsabilidades en la realización de controles de seguridad a las aerolíneas extranjeras que vuelan a Israel.

stories.headline: Polls show Latino voters shifting toward Democrats ahead of the midterms, driven by economic and immigration concerns

sources.body: President Donald Trump made major gains among Latino voters in 2024. Now, those same voters might cost Republicans control of Congress. Fifty-nine percent of Latino registered voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress, compared with 35% who favor Republican control, according to a new NBC News/Telemundo poll released Sunday. That 24-point gap for Democrats is twice the party’s lead compared to the September 2024 version of the poll. A separate CBS News/YouGov poll released Sunday also found Democrats ahead among Hispanic likely voters, with 60% backing a Democratic House candidate and 39% supporting a Republican. The findings threaten gains the GOP made in 2024, when Trump narrowed Democrats’ long-standing advantage among Latino voters. A POLITICO analysis of that year’s election results found that Trump improved his vote share by an average of more than 6 percentage points in majority-Hispanic counties, compared with 2020. With the midterms approaching, Republicans have made those gains central to their push to maintain control of the House. When Texas Republicans revealed their redistricting proposal last year , four of the five potential GOP pickup opportunities were in majority-Hispanic districts. Meanwhile, Trump’s overall approval rating among Latino registered voters stands at just 27% in the NBC/Telemundo poll, while 69% disapprove. On the economy specifically, 74% of Latino voters disapprove of Trump’s handling, while 78% disapprove of how he’s dealt with cost-of-living concerns. Nearly two-thirds, 65%, say Trump’s policies have hurt economic conditions. Inflation and cost of living rank as the most important issues facing the country for 33% of respondents, followed by government corruption at 22%. Another 10% named jobs and the economy. Economic frustration helped drive Latino voters toward Trump in 2024, with Democrats across the country suggesting in the aftermath of his victory that he was better able to connect with the voting bloc on financial issues. But now, Latino voters seem to favor Democrats over Republicans on the economy, 48% to 27%, and the cost of living, 45% compared to 26%. The war with Iran, now in its seventh month, is also weighing on voters’ perceptions of energy costs. In September, the average price of diesel hit a record $6.53, according to AAA . In the CBS survey, 91% of Hispanic registered voters attributed rising U.S. oil and gas prices to the conflict. Trump’s immigration crackdown is also putting vulnerable Republicans on the defensive . Rep. María Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.) released an ad in English and Spanish criticizing the administration for going “too far” on immigration and saying Hispanics who backed Trump in 2024 feel “betrayed.” In the days immediately following her ad, Trump told reporters that he still supported Salazar. “I’m very strong on the borders — and she isn’t,” Trump said. But the president later reposted a flurry of social media messages criticizing Salazar on Truth Social, including one calling for the Florida Republican’s replacement ahead of the midterms. In the NBC/Telemundo poll, 67% of Latino voters say Trump’s immigration enforcement has gone too far, compared with 22% who say he has taken the right approach. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Dissatisfaction with Trump and Republicans has not translated into broadly positive views of Democrats. According to the NBC poll, Latino voters remain nearly evenly divided on the Democratic Party, with 41% viewing it positively and 42% negatively. Negative views of the GOP, meanwhile, have climbed to 62%, up from 46% in September 2024. The NBC/Telemundo survey of 800 Latino registered voters was conducted Sept. 21-28 and has a margin of error of ±3.46%. The CBS/YouGov survey of 2,166 adults was conducted Sept. 30-Oct. 2, with a margin of error of ±2.5 points.
sources.headline: Trump’s gains among Latino voters slip ahead of midterms

stories.headline: Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton says his campaign messaging is being driven from Washington

sources.body: Ken Paxton is less than a month out from the conclusion of a D.C.-outsider campaign for a Texas U.S. Senate seat that he privately admitted is being run by Washington. “I’ve never been in a race where I felt less control over the campaign and, like, what issues are going to matter because it’s all coming — you know — from D.C.,” Paxton said during a small fundraising event last month, according to an audio recording obtained by POLITICO from a person in the room who does not support Paxton, and verified by another attendee. “I don’t control message or what we’re doing.” The lunch, hosted Sept. 24 in Washington by Chris Brinson and Susan Hirschmann of the D.C.-based lobbying firm Williams & Jensen, was attended by about a dozen people including Scott Kopple, VP of government relations at defense contractor BWXT. “Texas is a big state, and some of these issues obviously resonate with real — I’ll call real people — you know, like back home,” Kopple, who did not respond to a request for comment, said to some chuckles in the room. “I know you need money to get the message out and stuff, but how does this stuff translate?” Paxton replied saying: “I miss the days when I could go to, get around with all the people. But we have 32 million people, so let’s just say for the next 40 days I’m in front of 1,000 people a day — which I’m not — and that’s 40,000 people. Ten to 10.4 million people are gonna vote.” “But then it comes down to your messaging,” he continued, “which in a federal race comes from other people a lot of times, which you don’t control.” One attendee granted anonymity to discuss the private meeting said that Paxton never explicitly said he was referring to Trump’s team controlling his campaign, but “everybody knew what he was talking about.” The person said Paxton’s comments came amid a broader discussion about the national political environment. “I don’t have ability to change anything,” Paxton went on. “So I have to live with whatever I’ve got. So it is a challenge.” Paxton campaign adviser Nick Maddux said, “Campaigns don’t coordinate with super PACS and that’s obviously what AG Paxton was referring to,” in a statement to POLITICO. “AG Paxton is thankful for the support and knows how important Texas is to keeping the majority which is why he’s on the ground every day talking to Texas, raising money, and taking his message directly to the people including with his statewide television buy that started over this past weekend.” Neither Hirschmann nor Brinson responded to a request for comment. In an audio recording of the same meeting obtained by The New York Times , Paxton told attendees the midterm convention hosted by Trump in Texas last month “dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped. Right now, yeah, not good.” Maddux described the article as “manipulated nonsense.” Playbook hasn’t heard the contents of the rest of the hourlong meeting. The most recent New York Times/Siena poll has Paxton running 6 points behind Democratic challenger James Talarico. The private comments follow a bitter primary campaign waged against Republican incumbent John Cornyn, whom Paxton framed as a “Washington insider” and “RINO” while publicly aligning himself with Trump. “His money is coming from the D.C. establishment,” Paxton said of Cornyn while campaigning in Texas before the primary, the AP reported . “That’s how they always try to convince us from Washington with their money that we should select their person. Well, I’m not their person and I’m never going to be their person.” Paxton maintains a cash advantage heading into November and announced a $20 million ad buy last month. The Senate Leadership Fund, a top GOP super political action committee closely aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, pledged millions to back Paxton earlier in September. Like this content? Consider signing up for POLITICO's Playbook newsletter .
sources.headline: Campaign ‘all coming from DC,’ Paxton says

stories.headline: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez calls Spain’s general election for November 29 after setbacks over housing measures

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno hace balance de los logros de la coalición de izquierdas y lanza un dardo al Ejecutivo de Ayuso por el ático

Los españoles volverán a las urnas el 29 de noviembre . Pedro Sánchez ha decidido convocar las elecciones unos meses antes de lo previsto tras la derrota de los dos decretos sobre vivienda el pasado viernes. Sánchez ha resumido una legislatura muy difícil y ha pedido un apoyo mayor al proyecto progresista que quedó truncado el viernes al comprobar que no tiene una mayoría en el Congreso ni siquiera para aprobar medidas de emergencia sobre vivienda.

“Hace más de tres años las urnas decidieron volver a apostar por un Gobierno de coalición progresista. Nos ha tocado gestionar emergencias inéditas, navegar una coyuntura internacional muy difícil; hemos tenido que trabajar con un Congreso muy bronco. Hemos tenido que batirnos contra élites muy poderosas que no se presentan a las elecciones, pero quieren controlar nuestro país. Y con la peor oposición de la historia, que bloquea políticas que eran buenas para el país y las boicotea desde las autonomías”, ha explicado Sánchez.

“Hemos transferido a esos gobiernos autonómicos más recursos que nunca y ellos han comprado áticos y privatizado hospitales”, ha lanzado directo contra Isabel Díaz Ayuso. “A pesar de eso, España no ha dejado de avanzar; es la economía que más crece de la UE, el poder adquisitivo ha aumentado el triple que Francia o Alemania. Hemos ampliado becas, permisos de maternidad, dependencia, cartera del servicio de salud. Y hemos puesto en marcha una modernización profunda del país con el fondo Next Generation . Más de la mitad de nuestra energía procede de fuentes renovables. Y nos hemos negado a sacrificar el estado del bienestar en el altar del 5%”, ha insistido.

“Hemos hecho todo lo que estaba en nuestras manos, nos hemos esforzado por construir un mundo mejor. Apoyamos a Ucrania, a la UE, a la ONU, combatiendo a los tiranos, a los tecnooligarcas. Hemos duplicado nuestra ayuda a la cooperación internacional. Todo eso ha convertido a España en un referente mundial de paz, feminismo y prosperidad. Hemos cosechado los mejores datos económicos y sociales de cualquier gobierno. Es un hecho”, ha planteado Sánchez reivindicando esa buena imagen internacional.

“Quiero dar las gracias a la generosidad de otras fuerzas parlamentarias. Y gracias a la mayoría social que ha sacado lo mejor de sí misma. Sé que a esa mayoría le indigna lo que ha pasado en el Congreso. Sé que hemos cometido errores. Quedan muchas injusticias sociales que corregir, muchas metas en servicio público y vivienda. Lo cierto es que, para hacer más, necesitamos el apoyo de la gente; debemos lograr que el Parlamento nos dote de una mayoría progresista mucho más amplia. Por eso, tras informar al Rey, he decidido convocar Consejo Extraordinario para convocar elecciones el 29 de noviembre. Ahora depende de vosotros. El mundo se acerca a una época muy compleja”, ha rematado el presidente, en una escueta comparecencia en la que no ha explicado qué hará con los decretos decaídos. Ahora habrá un Consejo de Ministros extraordinario para rematar la convocatoria electoral. Y mañana se celebrará la reunión habitual de los martes, en la que se aprobarán los decretos de vivienda que tumbó el Congreso este viernes , aunque de momento se trabaja en La Moncloa para fijar si se presentará la misma redacción u otra similar.
sources.headline: Sánchez adelanta las elecciones al 29 de noviembre: “Necesitamos una mayoría progresista mucho más amplia”

El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez , ha anunciado este lunes la convocatoria de elecciones generales anticipadas para el próximo 29 de noviembre y ha asegurado que "ha llegado el momento de que los españoles decidáis qué futuro queréis".

Poco después de las 09.00 de la mañana, Sánchez ha despejado la incógnita que sobrevolaba todo el fin de semana tras el fracaso de los decretos en materia de vivienda el pasado viernes en el Congreso, tumbados por PP, Vox y Junts. Un fracaso que causó indignación en las calles que se movilizaban por el derecho a una vivienda digna tras el desahucio de Maricarmen la semana pasada y que le llevó a consultar estos últimos días a ministros y dirigentes socialistas sobre qué debía hacer.

El presidente lo decidió este domingo , cuando llamó al rey Felipe VI por la tarde para trasladarle que estaba decidido a convocar elecciones. Este lunes por la mañana ha informado también de su decisión a la vicepresidenta primera, Yolanda Díaz. Pero no ha sido hasta casi el final de su intervención de diez minutos cuando ha despejado las dudas.

"Tras informar al jefe del Estado , he decidido convocar u n Consejo de Ministros extraordinario esta misma mañana para disolver las Cortes y convocar elecciones generales, que se celebrarán el domingo 29 de noviembre de acuerdo con los plazos que establece la ley", ha comunicado en una declaración institucional sin preguntas desde el Palacio de La Moncloa. El Consejo de Ministros se celebra a partir de las 11.30 y no habrá rueda de prensa posterior.

La declaración no estaba prevista y se ha anunciado con una hora de antelación. De hecho, minutos después, fuentes de la Presidencia del Gobierno anulaban la agenda que Sánchez tenía para este lunes, como su asistencia al XXIX Congreso de Empresa Familiar, prevista para esta mañana en Madrid.

Sánchez, que ha admitido que su Ejecutivo ha cometido "errores " y no ha logrado hacer "todo" lo que se había propuesto, ha recalcado que para avanzar en todo lo que queda por hacer en materia de vivienda y frente a otras "injusticias" y causas sociales necesita una mayoría más amplia en el Congreso: " Para hacer más, necesitamos renovar y ampliar el apoyo de la gente ".

"Sé que en parte de esa mayoría social hoy hay insatisfacción . Les indigna ver cómo sus intereses son pisoteados en el Parlamento en beneficio de unos pocos", ha manifestado el presidente en referencia a los últimos decretos en materia de vivienda.

Pero ha recalcado que para seguir avanzando "debemos movilizarnos y lograr que el Parlamento nos dote una mayoría mucho más amplia , progresista, con la que doblegar las élites, conquistar los derechos sociales y seguir transformando España", ha defendido.

El jefe del Ejecutivo ha advertido, sin embargo, de que "el mundo se asoma a una época muy compleja " de transición y " tensiones ", de cambios sociales y tecnológicos "muy disruptivos" como ocurre con la IA y de "emergencia climática". Una época, ha resumido, de "grandes peligros" , pero también de "grandes oportunidades".

sources.body:
Pedro Sánchez ha decidido adelantar las elecciones generales  y poner fin a una legislatura que el viernes quedó prácticamente sin mayoría parlamentaria. El presidente del Gobierno ha tomado la decisión después de un fin de semana de reflexión, llamadas y reuniones en el que la derrota de los decretos de vivienda en el Congreso y las multitudinarias movilizaciones del sábado han terminado de  dibujar el escenario.  Las urnas se abrirán el 29 de noviembre, de acuerdo con los plazos que establece la ley.

Sánchez comunicó durante la tarde de ayer al Rey su decisión de disolver las Cortes y convocar elecciones generales. El siguiente paso será la reunión extraordinaria del Consejo de Ministros, prevista para las 11.30 horas, en la que se aprobará formalmente la convocatoria electoral. La reunión no estará seguida, al contrario de lo habitual, de la rueda de prensa posterior del Ejecutivo.

La vivienda se transforma así, de golpe, en el gran eje de la contienda electoral. Lo que hasta el viernes era una carpeta sectorial es hoy la principal grieta socioeconómica del país, después de que el rechazo conjunto de PP, Vox y Junts colisionara frontalmente con la presión de la calle. La Moncloa busca rentabilizar el golpe y convertir la cita del 29-N en un plebiscito directo sobre el mercado inmobiliario.

El balance que Sánchez ha hecho de sus tres años de Gobierno ha tenido dos caras. La primera, la de los resultados que el presidente reivindica -crecimiento económico, creación de empleo y políticas sociales- y que le permiten sostener que, pese a las dificultades, el Ejecutivo “no ha dejado de trabajar” y España “no ha dejado de avanzar”. La segunda, la de una agenda que considera todavía inconclusa. “Aún quedan muchas injusticias que corregir, muchas metas sociales que conquistar y muchos problemas que resolver”, ha admitido, con la desigualdad, los servicios públicos y, sobre todo, el acceso a la vivienda entre los principales asuntos pendientes.

El marco trazado por el presidente no deja espacio al centro: o una “ola ultraderechista que involuciona” o una España como “baluarte de justicia social”. Sánchez ha resumido así la disyuntiva que pretende llevar a las urnas: “Si queréis que nuestro país retroceda o continúe avanzando”.

El líder del Ejecutivo ha aprovechado además su intervención para arremeter contra la oposición, a la que ha acusado de haber protagonizado “la peor oposición que ha conocido nuestra historia democrática”. Sánchez ha reprochado al PP su “falta de sentido de Estado” y su estrategia de bloqueo, y ha asegurado que su Gobierno ha tenido que enfrentarse también a “élites económicas y sociales muy poderosas” que, según ha dicho, pretenden seguir controlando el país sin presentarse a las elecciones.

El Gobierno tampoco piensa abandonar la batalla por la vivienda durante el periodo que conduzca a las urnas. Fuentes del Ejecutivo apuntan a La Vanguardia que prepara un plan de choque que pasará por recuperar en un inminente Consejo de Ministros los dos decretos que decayeron el viernes, bien para llevarlos de nuevo al Congreso o bien para intentar vehicularlos a través de la Diputación Permanente una vez disueltas las Cortes.

Con las Cortes disueltas, el apoyo de Junts resulta irrelevante en dicho órgano del Congreso

El Consejo de Ministros ordinario aprobará mañana unos decretos de vivienda similares a los que tumbó el Congreso este viernes, no exactamente los mismos, aunque aún se trabaja en La Moncloa para ver cuál será la redacción final. La idea con la que trabaja el Gobierno es la de que estos decretos se convaliden en la Diputación Permanente, donde el voto de Junts es irrelevante. Si el PNV mantiene su voto, podría salir adelante el llamado “decreto Maricarmen”, que impide los desahucios de personas vulnerables, pero no el segundo, el que haría permanentes los contratos de alquiler.

Fuentes del Gobierno señalan que no está previsto llevar exactamente los mismos decretos, algo que podría generar problemas jurídicos porque los tumbó el pleno y los convalidaría un órgano menor, sino unos con modificaciones, algo que tendría unas consecuencias jurídicas diferentes pero habría que volver a negociar con los socios.

Precisamente una de las grandes cuestiones que tiene que resolver el Gobierno, y de la que Pedro Sánchez no dijo nada en su comparecencia, es qué pasa con los decretos decaídos. En La Moncloa están estudiando con detalle la fórmula jurídica más adecuada para intentar recuperar el máximo posible, sobre todo del primer decreto, el del escudo antidesahucios, el que estaba pactado con PNV, Coalición Canaria y con Junts, según el Gobierno, y tenía posibilidades de salir.

Aunque se produzca el adelanto electoral, el Ejecutivo no está en funciones —eso es después de los comicios—, sino en plenitud de atribuciones, y por tanto podría aprobar de nuevo los decretos iguales o parecidos. Lo que sí sucedería es que las Cortes estarían disueltas y entonces la convalidación de esos decretos pasaría a depender de la Diputación Permanente, ya no del pleno. Y ahí el Gobierno tiene una gran ventaja: el voto de Junts es irrelevante.

El Ejecutivo necesita 35 votos, que dan la mayoría absoluta de los 69 que componen ese órgano, más reducido que el pleno y pensado para decidir en lugar de este fuera de los periodos de sesiones o cuando las Cortes están disueltas. El PSOE tiene 25 y Sumar 6, así que le faltarían cuatro para alcanzar la mayoría. Bastaría con que votaran a favor EH Bildu, ERC, Podemos y PNV, que ya apoyaron el primero de los decretos en el Congreso, para que saliera adelante. El rechazo de Junts sería irrelevante aquí. El que sí decaería es el segundo decreto, por la oposición del PNV.
sources.headline: El Consejo de Ministros aprobará mañana unos decretos de vivienda similares a los que cayeron para que los vote la Diputación Permanente

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez 

“Disolvemos para hacer políticas de vivienda. Las que podamos hacer ya, las haremos”, advierten fuentes de la Moncloa a La Vanguardia . Este lunes, el Consejo de Ministros extraordinario convocado de urgencia por Pedro Sánchez aprueba el adelanto electoral para el próximo 29 de noviembre que ha anunciado el presidente del Gobierno, y la disolución de las Cortes Generales de esta legislatura. Pero la previsión es que el Consejo de Ministros ordinario que se volverá a reunir mañana aprobará, en todo o en parte, los reales decretos ley que el Congreso tumbó el pasado viernes, con los votos del PP, Vox, UPN y Junts.

La diferencia, no obstante, es que, una vez disueltas las Cortes, se activa en el Congreso la diputación permanente, donde operan mayorías distintas a las del pleno en las que eran imprescindibles los siete votos de Junts para que el Gobierno sumara una mayoría absoluta con los grupos de la investidura. Para que la diputación permanente del Congreso convalide las medidas sobre vivienda que volverá a aprobar mañana el Consejo de Ministros ya no serán imprescindibles los votos de la formación de Carles Puigdemont.

Desde que Junts tumbó el pasado viernes el decreto ley que incluía, entre otras iniciativas, una moratoria de los desahucios y una prórroga de los contratos de alquiler de vivienda –que finalmente también votaron a favor el PNV y CC, además del PSOE, Sumar, ERC, EH Bildu, Podemos o el BNG-, Sánchez no solo contempló el adelanto electoral anunciado este lunes, sino que aseguró que su prioridad era reflotar estas medidas, para no dejar en la estacada a las personas más vulnerables y dar respuesta a las protestas sociales que se dispararon tras el desahucio de Maricarmen en Madrid. La opción, aseguraron en la Moncloa, no podía ser solo dejar esta crisis de la vivienda a la espera de que se celebraran unas elecciones adelantadas. Así que la determinación de Sánchez es volver a aprobarlas.

Esta vez ya no será necesaria la urgencia de la última vez para llevar estos decretos de vivienda al Congreso. Una vez aprobadas mañana las nuevas iniciativas, se abrirá un plazo de un mes para convalidarlas, esta vez, en la diputación permanente del Congreso. De esta manera, además, el Gobierno podrá mantener vivo el debate sobre la vivienda prácticamente hasta que arranque la campaña electoral del 29-N. En el Ejecutivo aseguran que este es un debate que moviliza a la izquierda y perjudica a la derecha. “Lo van a pagar”, advirtieron en la Moncloa al PP, Vox y Junts, cuando tumbaron en el Congreso las medidas con las que pretendían paliar la crisis de la vivienda y el drama de los desahucios.

Madrid, 1966. Redactor de La Vanguardia en Madrid desde 1997

Pedro Sánchez y Miriam Nogueras, Junts. Pleno extraordinario para convalidación de los decretos sobre vivienda, en el Congreso de los Diputados. / José Luis Roca

Al comienzo de cada legislatura hay una votación clave en el Congreso, casi tan importante como la de investir presidente a alguno de los candidatos. Se trata de la elección de la Mesa del Congreso . Quien controla este órgano controla la actividad parlamentaria y, además, determina también las mayorías en las comisiones y en la Diputación Permanente . A comienzos de esta legislatura, PSOE y Sumar se garantizaron una aritmética parlamentaria beneficiosa en estos espacios y ahora, con las elecciones ya convocadas, Pedro Sánchez va a echar mano de aquella decisión para esquivar el veto de Junts que tumbó las medidas de vivienda y que, previsiblemente, volverá a aprobar el Consejo de Ministros este martes .

La disolución de las Cortes anunciada por Sánchez pone fin a la actividad parlamentaria ordinaria y, desde este martes, cuando se publique la convocatoria electoral en el BOE, y hasta la constitución de las nuevas Cámaras tras los comicios, todo queda en manos de la Diputación Permanente . Así, el Ejecutivo podría aprobar un decreto ley con las medidas de vivienda que fueron rechazadas la pasada semana y sería este órgano, donde Junts no tiene capacidad de veto , el que tendría que convalidar el texto.

Las urnas arrojan una proporción de diputados que componen los 350 escaños de la Cámara. Sin embargo, es la Mesa del Congreso la que, después, traslada esas mayorías a las comisiones y a la Diputación Permanente, de tal forma que los grupos parlamentarios estén representados "en proporción a su importancia numérica", según el Reglamento del Congreso. Ahora bien, traducir los porcentajes exactos a un órgano de alrededor de 60 miembros no es sencillo .

Ante esta situación, PSOE y Sumar, con mayoría en la Mesa, impusieron una aritmética que les beneficiaba . Si en el pleno necesitan a todos sus aliados -ERC, Junts, EH Bildu, PNV y Podemos- para alcanzar la mayoría absoluta y solo pueden permitirse una abstención para superar la mayoría simple, en la Diputación Permanente pueden prescindir del apoyo de uno de sus socios, incluso aunque vote en contra .

El reparto, aprobado por la Mesa del Congreso el 3 de noviembre de 2023, establece que este órgano estará compuesto por 68 diputados más la presidenta de la Cámara : el PP tiene 27 sillas ; el PSOE, 25 (contando a Francina Armengol); Sumar y Vox, seis cada uno ; y el resto de grupos -ERC, Junts, EH Bildu, PNV y Grupo Mixto- disponen de un escaño cada uno. El del Grupo Mixto está en manos de la líder de Podemos, Ione Belarra .

Así, si el Consejo de Ministros aprueba mañana un real decreto ley con medidas de vivienda, el órgano encargado de votarlo sería la Diputación Permanente. El artículo 57 del Reglamento del Congreso deja claro que entre sus funciones está "asumir todas las facultades que en relación con los Decretos-leyes atribuye al Congreso de los Diputados el artículo 86 de la Constitución". Es decir, la convalidación o derogación de esos textos .

stories.headline: Torrential rain and flooding disrupt transport across Barcelona and Catalunya, with fresh alerts along the coast

sources.body:
A las 10:00 de la mañana de este lunes los vecinos de Barcelona y de L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, entre otros municipios han recibido un mensaje de Protección Civil de la Generalitat de Cataluña alertando de lluvias torrenciales hasta este mediodía y en el que pedía que restringieran su movilidad y evitar las actividades en el exterior, no acceder a zonas inundables como ríos y rieras y no bajar a subterráneos. Todo ello tras un dramático fin de semana en el que esas lluvias torrenciales han dejado dos personas muertas .

Antes, la primera alerta Es-Alert para pedir precaución en la movilidad ha llegado al área del Maresme y el Vallès Oriental hacia las 08.00 horas y hacia las 09.30 horas otro mensaje para pedir el confinamiento de los vecinos de la comarca del Vallès Oriental por riesgo de desbordamiento de rieras.

Muy complicado está siendo este lunes en esta región en las comarcas del Barcelonès, Alt Penedès, Garraf, Baix Llobregat, Vallès Occidental, Maresme y la Selva, que también han sido alertadas.

Las lluvias han provocado problemas en todos los transportes, el aéreo, el ferroviario y por carretera , en una jornada en la que en el aeropuerto de Josep Tarradellas Barcelona-El Prat se ha registrado un total de al menos 30 vuelos cancelados, aunque esa cifra puede aumentar.

El temporal persiste este lunes con nueve comunidades bajo aviso por lluvias y tormentas, con la situación más adversa en Cataluña por precipitaciones torrenciales , hasta 90 litros por metro cuadrado en una hora, en el arranque de una semana marcada por los chubascos en amplias zonas del país, que irán perdiendo intensidad a partir del miércoles.

El presidente de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, ha pedido "máxima precaución" ante las lluvias torrenciales que durante la mañana han provocado varias inundaciones en el área de Barcelona , en un episodio que "no estaba previsto" por los modelos meteorológicos y que ha "sobrepasado cualquier predicción".

Tras las intensas tormentas que durante el fin de semana han dejado registros históricos de acumulación de agua en Cataluña, este nuevo episodio de lluvias torrenciales, con Granollers (Barcelona) como epicentro, ha provocado varias inundaciones, también en la ciudad de Barcelona, ha colapsado la movilidad y ha puesto a varios ríos y rieras al límite.

En un mensaje en su cuenta de X, Illa, que participa en la reunión del Centro de Emergencias (CECAT) para abordar los "graves efectos" que estas lluvias torrenciales han provocado en varias comarcas, ha admitido que la situación meteorológica "ha sobrepasado cualquier predicción: Este episodio de lluvias no estaba previsto por los modelos meteorológicos".

Illa, que ha resaltado que los servicios de emergencias están atendiendo "sin descanso" los avisos relacionados con estas lluvias torrenciales, ha pedido también a la ciudadanía que evite acercarse a ríos, rieras, sótanos y zonas bajas y que si el agua llega a la altura de su casa suban a las plantas superiores de los edificios.

El temporal de este lunes ha obligado a cortar la circulación en algunos tramos del metro de Barcelona, en algunas líneas de Rodalies, ha inundado partes de la Roda de Barcelona y de varias carreteras y ha dificultado la movilidad en la corona metropolitana.

EL PERIÓDICO ofrece en este directo la última hora del tráfico y la movilidad en Catalunya , con especial atención a las graves afectaciones provocadas por el episodio de lluvias del fin de semana. Sigue en tiempo real las retenciones, carreteras cortadas, desprendimientos, inundaciones e incidencias que están complicando los desplazamientos, especialmente en Barcelona y su área metropolitana.

El directo recoge también las importantes afectaciones en Rodalies y otros servicios de transporte público , así como los cambios en el servicio, las líneas afectadas y las alternativas para los viajeros. Toda la información sobre el estado de las carreteras y del transporte público, además de los avisos y recomendaciones que puedan condicionar la movilidad durante la jornada.

TMB informa de que la L3 del metro de Barcelona recupera la circulación con normalidad después de haber estado interrumpida entre Passeig de Gràcia y Vall d’Hebron por las afectaciones de las lluvias.

La R17 presta servicio entre Barcelona Estació de França y Tarragona . Los viajeros disponen de un servicio alternativo por carretera entre Tarragona y Salou-PortAventura .

En la R14 , los trenes circulan entre Lleida-Pirineus y Les Borges Blanques y también entre Reus y Barcelona Estació de França . El tramo entre Lleida-Pirineus y Reus se cubre con un servicio alternativo por carretera .

Protección Civil ha enviado un ES-Alert a Santa Cristina d’Aro, Castell d’Aro, Platja d’Aro, S’Agaró y Sant Feliu de Guíxols (Baix Empordà, Girona) ante el riesgo de incremento del caudal del río Ridaura y de los barrancos cercanos .

El aviso pide a la población protegerse en el interior de los edificios y evitar desplazamientos, sótanos y zonas bajas . En caso de peligro, Protección Civil recomienda llamar al 112 .

Una avería de un vehículo en el arcén provoca retenciones en la AP-7 , a su paso por Cerdanyola del Vallès , en sentido sur.

Un accidente mantiene un carril cortado en la AP-7 , en enlace con la A-2 en Martorell . La incidencia genera circulación con congestión en este punto.

La mejora de las condiciones permite que el Teleférico de Montjuïc vuelva a funcionar con normalidad, después de haber permanecido fuera de servicio por las afectaciones de las lluvias.

El metro de Barcelona mantiene varias líneas afectadas por las lluvias. La L3 no presta servicio entre Passeig de Gràcia y Vall d’Hebron y la estación de Liceu permanece fuera de servicio. La L4 está cortada entre Maragall y Via Júlia .

También siguen interrumpidas la L9N , entre Onze de Setembre y Bon Pastor , y la L10N , entre Onze de Setembre y Llefià . Las líneas L5, L9S, L10S y L11 funcionan con normalidad, al igual que el Funicular de Montjuïc .

Además, permanecen fuera de servicio una andana de la L1 en Rambla Just Oliveras y otra de la L2 en Sant Roc .

También hay varios accesos y vestíbulos cerrados en distintas estaciones, entre ellos Zona Universitària, Glòries, Plaça Eivissa, Tajo d’Horta, Can Cuiàs, Torre Baró-Vallbona, Canyelles, Pubilla Cases y Diagonal .

stories.headline: Flooding damages Barcelona schools, forcing some students to eat in classrooms as facilities are assessed

sources.body: Els aiguats torrencials d’aquest dilluns al matí han afectat algunes escoles de Barcelona . Malgrat que pràcticament totes han obert portes a les 9 h sense incidències, poca estona després la pluja ha afectat algunes instal·lacions . És el cas de l’Escola Poeta Foix , al barri del Putxet i el Farró. La planta soterrani, on hi ha el menjador i les instal·lacions de l’AFA, ha quedat negada d’aigua . El centre ja ha avisat que no es podrà oferir el servei en aquest espai i que els alumnes que es quedin, hauran de dinar a les aules. Algunes lamenten que no és la primera vegada que viuen una situació semblant, malgrat que fa poc temps que s’havien fet obres per renovar l’espai. El Consorci d’Educació explica que s’hi enviaran tècnics per avaluar i solucionar la situació. Algunes famílies s’han organitzat per intentar treure aigua de l’espai i que les afectacions no vagin a més. També hi ha hagut filtracions d’aigua a l’ Escola Bressol El Gat Negre, a Gràcia. Al barri de la Trinitat Vella, al districte de Sant Andreu, l’aiguat també ha provocat problemes al CEE El Nus. La pluja ha afectat la cuina, el menjador i dues aules i ha malmès molt material. L’activitat lectiva continuarà, però els alumnes hauran de dinar a les aules. Al Raval , després dels afectes del temporal del cap de setmana i les pluges del matí, a l’escola Salle Comtal s’han trobat amb el menjador i el gimnàs plens d’aigua . Amb l’ajuda de l’alumnat han estat treballant al llarg de tot el matí per eixugar-la. Les aules, com que es troben més elevades que el nivell del terra, no s’han vist afectades i es poden fer les classes amb certa normalitat. Altres escoles de la ciutat també han viscut una situació similar i han hagut treballar per treure l’aigua dels centres, com l’Escola IPSE. El Consorci d’Educació afirma que està recollint totes les incidències per poder avaluar l’abast de les afectacions als centres escolars de la ciutat. La escuela Poeta Foix, del barrio del Putxet de Barcelona, inundada per la rotura de una cañería de aguas fecales / FOTO Y VÍDEO: CEDIDO A ACN POR TONI GM

La escuela Poeta Foix, en el barrio del Putxet de Barcelona, ha vuelto a inundarse este lunes por la mañana , apenas unos días después de sufrir un episodio similar. Esta vez, el desbordamiento de una tubería externa de aguas fecales ha provocado que el agua entre con fuerza en el centro hasta alcanzar la altura de las rodillas en algunas zonas. La presidenta de la AFA, Clara Bonet, ha explicado a la ACN que el problema ya se produjo la semana pasada, coincidiendo con las abundantes lluvias, y que este lunes se ha repetido. La inundación ha afectado al patio, al comedor semisubterráneo y a varias salas , dejando parte de la escuela impracticable.

El episodio ha sorprendido a los alumnos cuando ya se encontraban dentro del centro . Ante el avance del agua, la escuela ha pedido a las familias que tengan posibilidad de hacerlo que acudan a recoger a sus hijos . Los alumnos que permanezcan en el colegio tendrán que comer en las aulas, ya que el comedor ha quedado inutilizable. El centro está situado junto a la calle Balmes y algunas voces relacionan el desbordamiento de la tubería con las obras que se están realizando en la calle , aunque por el momento no se ha establecido oficialmente esa relación.

La situación ha generado también malestar entre las familias. Bonet ha lamentado que el Consorcio de Educación no pueda atender al centro este lunes debido a las incidencias registradas en otras escuelas. Desde el Consorcio, sin embargo, confirman la inundación y aseguran que el colegio sí está siendo atendido por la técnica de gestión territorial y el referente técnico de zona .

El incidente de la escuela Poeta Foix se produce en plena polémica por la decisión de mantener abiertos muchos centros educativos este lunes pese a los avisos meteorológicos y a los efectos de las lluvias torrenciales de los últimos días.

El sindicato docente USTEC , mayoritario en la escuela pública catalana, ha criticado que numerosos colegios e institutos hayan abierto sus puertas por la mañana a pesar de los avisos por lluvia y de la situación vivida durante el fin de semana .

A juicio del sindicato, en las zonas castigadas por las lluvias torrenciales y donde este lunes continuaban activos nuevos avisos, los centros «no deberían haber abierto» . «Ante la incertidumbre sobre cómo se encontrarían los centros y con nuevos avisos activos, había que actuar con la máxima precaución», ha defendido. USTEC sostiene además que el alcance de las incidencias podría ser mayor de lo que reflejan inicialmente los datos oficiales. El sindicato advierte de que la lista de centros afectados que facilita el Departamento de Educación sigue creciendo y asegura que los colegios e institutos con problemas acabarán siendo «muchos más». También denuncia que mantener la actividad presencial ha obligado a desplazarse a miles de trabajadores en un contexto meteorológico complicado y considera que la apertura de los centros ha podido comprometer " la movilidad y la seguridad" del personal educativo .
